In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNase P holicenzyme is a very large complex, which is highly flexible and dynamic in nature.
RNase P is a complex of two subunits (RNA and protein) that are held together by a network of non-covalent interactions.

the RNA subunit of bacterial RNase P has an L-shaped structure, with a large domain (domain I) consisting of a five-helix junction (5-hJ) and an adjacent four-way junction (4-WJ) and a small domain (domain II) consisting of a four-helix junction (4-hJ) and a four-way junction (2-WJ).

The main takeaway from our work is that

the protein subunits of type A and type B RNase P are structurally similar and that the RNA subunits are arranged in a manner that allows the two proteins to bind to the RNA in the same orientation, regardless of the RNA sequence.
the RNase P protein subunit is a flexible molecule that is able to adopt different conformations in the presence of the RNA subunit.

the RNase P RNA subunit of the E.coli RNAP holoenzyme has two distinct binding sites for its cofactor protein: one site for the protein's N-terminal domain and a second site for the protein C-terminal domain.
